g.text: Only two of these seven studies are evidence
On a common basis, most of the precedents we are quoted are about a
different intervention or a different sector.
What changed, and what it found
Real hours cut at full pay; 92% still
89% still on reduced hours a year
on; the one firm that stopped was a
held. Veal: 61 of 66 sites cut only
A right to compress 38 hours into
four days; hours and pay unchanged
the authors call it a proof of concept
Dark: evidence about a firm like ours. Slate: partly relevant. Grey: a different intervention or a different sector.
The same trials are read as a transformative national success and as a
one-to-three-hour cut whose national legacy is 35 minutes a week.
The council reports 21 of 24 services improved or stayed the same and a saving
of nearly £400,000 a year; the independent evaluation reports 11 outcomes
better, 2 worse and the rest indistinguishable, and cannot prove causation.
Sources: Autonomy · Alda/Autonomy Iceland · Veal (UTS) · Belgian Labour Deal · Portugal (2024) · Germany (2024)
